name: Plus-Minus Jass
description: Plus-Minus Jass is a Swiss Jass variant for 3 or 4 players. Cards are dealt equally and played as in Mittlere or Molotow. Scoring is by sticks only (no potatoes). The first player to score 7 sticks wins. If everyone scores under 100 card points, the players with most and least points each score one stick; if someone takes 100 or more, only the player with least points scores a stick.

history.origins: Plus-Minus Jass is a Swiss Jass variant documented alongside Mittlere and Molotow in English-language card game literature. It uses the same deal and trick-taking rules as Mittlere (3 players) or Molotow (4 players) but scores only sticks; the first to 7 sticks wins.
timeline: Traditional: Part of Swiss Jass family
Modern: Documented with Mittlere and Molotow in card game literature
history.cultural: Played in Switzerland and among Jass enthusiasts; available in Michael Gasser's Jass!! program.
history.evolution: Derived from Mittlere and Molotow; simplifies scoring to sticks only with no potatoes.

setup.players: 3 or 4 players, each playing for themselves.
setup.deck: 36-card Jass deck (Ace, King, Ober, Under, Banner, 9, 8, 7, 6 in four suits). Can use standard deck with cards below 6 removed.
setup.dealing: All cards dealt equally: 9 each for 4 players, 12 each for 3 players, in packets of 3. Deal and play anticlockwise.
setup.equipment: 36-card Jass deck or modified standard deck; scoring tokens or slate for sticks.

rules.objective: Be the first to score 7 sticks. Score sticks by having the highest or lowest card-point total when everyone is under 100 points, or by having the only different total when others tie; if someone takes 100 or more, only the player with least points scores.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's right leads. Must follow suit if possible. First time a player cannot follow suit and plays another suit, that suit becomes trumps for the hand. Once trumps are set, must follow suit or play a trump; may play a lower trump only when void in the led suit. Trick winner leads to the next trick. Card points: Ace 11, King 4, Ober 3, Under 2, Banner 10, 9/8/7/6 zero; in trump Under 20, 9 14. Last trick bonus 5; total 157 points.
keyRules: First void play sets trumps for the hand
Under 100: most and least card points score one stick each
100 or more: only least points scores one stick
Puur (Under of trumps) need not be played when trumps led and it is your only trump

strategy.basic: Aim for either most or least card points when everyone is under 100; avoid the middle. Ensure you win at least one trick when possible.
strategy.intermediate: Control when trumps are established by choosing when to void. Win early tricks to control the lead. Preserve 6s and Aces.
strategy.advanced: Track suit distribution and card points. Calculate whether to push for most or least points. In 4-player ties, understand stick-in-abeyance rules.
tips: Under 100 points: most and least each get a stick
Someone takes 100+: only least points gets a stick
First to 7 sticks wins; continue until clear leader if tie at 7

variations.name: Three players
variations.description: 12 cards each; scoring rules same as 4-player.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No engine overrides; variant only changes player count and deal size.

variations.name: Four-player tie for most or least
variations.description: When two tie for most or least card points, neither scores but one stick is held in abeyance until the next hand when only one of them scores, then given to that player.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No engine overrides; variant only adds tie-abeyance rule to base scoring.

scoring.description: Sticks only. Under 100 card points: most and least each score one stick. If someone takes 100 or more: only least points scores one stick. First to 7 sticks wins; if several reach 7 in same hand, continue until clear leader.
scoring.winCondition: First player to score 7 sticks wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: Swiss Jass for 3 or 4 players. Score sticks only; first to 7 sticks wins. Most and least card points under 100 score one stick each.
